summary: Elevated 5xx rates traced to slow TLS handshakes on edge causing connection pile-up and upstream runtime resets for a dedicated tenant
description:
Issue summary: Since ~2026-03-14T02:20Z LexiAI has observed a sharp increase in 5xx responses from our hosted API. Errors surface mostly as 502/504 at the API gateway and increased SIGABRT/exit events on serving runtime workers downstream. Early telemetry shows long TLS handshake latencies on a subset of edge nodes which caused connection queueing and amplified retry storms against the runtime fleet.

Initial impact: Customer reported degraded request success rate for live inference routes and several dropped streaming sessions. Latency and failure spikes coincide with tenant traffic bursts during daily model prefetches.
impact:
- Customer-facing errors: 18% error rate at peak for LexiAI routes in us-east-1 (normal <0.5%).
- Observable symptoms: 502/504 at API gateway, increased runtime worker restarts, transient OOMs and connection reset logs.
- Business impact: Live features degraded for paying dedicated tenant; potential SLA breaches if not remediated.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Target LexiAI tenant routes in prod us-east-1 during scheduled prefetch window (observed at ~02:15-02:35Z).
2) Send concurrent inference traffic at historical high-concurrency profile (approx. 1200 rps sustained for 3 minutes).
3) Observe API gateway 502/504 rates and runtime worker restart counts in monitoring dashboards.
4) Capture tcpdump/tls handshake timing on affected edge node and inspect upstream connection resets from runtime proxies.
logs: api-gateway: [2026-03-14T02:22:11Z] upstream_connection_error: TLS handshake timeout after 12.1s (edge-node-7b)
serving-runtime: [2026-03-14T02:23:18Z] runtime_manager: worker_pid=1248 exited SIGABRT (oom="false") - last_request_duration_ms=15423
serving-runtime: [2026-03-14T02:24:01Z] runtime_proxy: upstream_reset_by_peer during response write code=RST_STREAM
investigation_notes: Telemetry: TLS handshake p95 on ~20% of edge nodes in us-east-1 rose from 40ms -> 5-12s starting 02:15Z; these nodes show increased system load and elevated open file handles.
Correlation: Spikes align with LexiAI prefetch job and tenant burst on dedicated capacity pool; dedicated pool autoscaler not scaling fast enough and queued connections accumulated at edge layer.

Hypothesis 1: Edge TLS handshake slowness (likely userland crypto or kernel throttling) caused accept backlog and proxy queueing, leading to API gateway timeouts and fanout retries to runtime causing resource pressure and runtime restarts.
Hypothesis 2: A small percentage of clients reusing incompatible TLS session parameters triggered expensive handshake paths on a subset of edge nodes (observed client hello metrics).

Quick checks done: validated node-level kernel dmesg (no obvious OOM), checked ip_vs conntrack counts, verified no recent deployment to edge fleet in the 24h window, compared metrics with other regions (not affected).
comments: 2026-03-14T03:05Z - Ethan Morales: Reached out to SREs to isolate edge-node cohort. Spun up new edge instances with connection reaper changes to test traffic routing.
2026-03-14T03:20Z - SRE on #support: Temporarily throttled LexiAI prefetch traffic at the API gateway per-tenant policy to reduce pressure. Notified customer via support channel.
2026-03-14T03:45Z - Customer (LexiAI): Confirmed immediate reduction in observed errors after throttling but reported longer end-to-end latency for some requests.
2026-03-14T04:10Z - Aisha Patel: Adding linked incident SUP-720304 for historical autoscaler-liveness context; opening runtime PR to guard against successive retries.
root_cause_summary: A subset of edge nodes experienced pathological TLS handshake latencies (5-12s) under burst load, causing connection queueing at the API gateway. The queueing amplified fanout to the serving runtime, overwhelming worker pools and triggering unstable behavior/resets. The underlying trigger appears to be expensive handshake paths combined with insufficient edge connection reaping and a lagging dedicated autoscaler for the tenant pool.
resolution:
Mitigation performed: 1) Applied emergency per-tenant rate-limiter to LexiAI prefetch routes to cap concurrent prefetches. 2) Re-routed new traffic away from the affected edge cohort and performed rolling restart of 6 edge nodes in us-east-1 to clear handshake state. 3) Increased API gateway short-circuit timeout from 10s -> 6s for handshake phase to fail fast and prevent long queue retention. 4) Deployed temporary change to connection reaper aggressive mode on edge proxies.

Observed result: 5xx rates dropped from 18% -> 0.8% within 20 minutes and runtime restarts subsided. Customer notified of mitigations and workaround while permanent fix is delivered.
follow_up_actions: 1) Engineering: Ship PR to add per-connection TLS handshake timeout and more aggressive session resumption checks on edge (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge/pull/2896).
2) Platform: Adjust dedicated autoscaler warmup thresholds for prefetch patterns (task assigned to infra squad).
3) SRE: Add synthetic TLS handshake healthchecks and an alert when p95 handshake > 500ms on >10% of edge nodes.
4) Product/CS: Coordinate with LexiAI to smooth prefetch schedule or provide a recommended concurrency cap for dedicated tenants during model warmups.
5) Runbook: Update confluence page with steps for per-tenant throttling and edge cohort isolation procedure.
notes_for_postmortem: Postmortem to include timeline of events, edge kernel/userland metrics around handshake, autoscaler timings, and a proposal for default keepalive and handshake timeouts. Recommend a test plan to reproduce handshake path costs with client hello variants.
